chunks.title: Computer Science
chunks.heading: Computer Science
chunks.content: Computer Science is the broad index for computing-related topics in the vault. Full Notes should normally use one of the more focused topics below instead of this root topic.

chunks.title: Computer Science
chunks.heading: Computer Science > Overview Chapter
chunks.content: Computer science studies how information can be represented, transformed, and used to produce reliable behavior. Its subject is larger than programming alone. It includes the logical foundations of computation, the engineering of software, the behavior of complex systems, the design of human-facing interfaces, the construction of learning and conversational machines, and the production of interactive systems such as games. These areas are connected by a common question: how can a desired capability be expressed precisely enough that a computational system can perform it, while remaining useful and understandable in the world where it operates?

chunks.title: Computer Science
chunks.heading: Computer Science > Overview Chapter > From logical rules to system behavior
chunks.content:
At the most abstract level, [[Formal Logic]] provides a language for propositions, valid inference, equivalence, and Boolean operations. These ideas make it possible to state conditions precisely and reason about whether a conclusion follows from a set of premises. Programs turn this formal structure into executable behavior, but useful programs are rarely isolated collections of rules. [[Software Engineering]] adds requirements, architecture, implementation practices, testing, documentation, and iteration so that software can remain dependable as its size and context change.

[[Theory of Computation]] examines the formal machines and languages used to distinguish what can be recognized, decided, or computed. Automata, grammars, Turing machines, and reductions connect logical descriptions to precise limits on computational procedures.

[[Algorithmic Methods]] describes the finite procedures that make computational behavior explicit. An algorithm receives input, follows precise control structures, and produces output, while complexity analysis asks how its time and storage needs grow. Search, sorting, graphs, matrix methods, PageRank, and neural-network training show how a good representation exposes structure that a procedure can exploit. This separates the abstract method from any one program or computer while still explaining why some correct methods are practical and others are overwhelmed by scale.

[[Social and Complex Network Analytics]] studies computational systems whose information lies in both entities and their connections. It joins geometric and multilayer graph representations with scalable dataflows, behavior and popularity models, misinformation and rumor analysis, and application-specific interpretation. The topic shows why large-network computation must coordinate storage, algorithms, statistical evidence, temporal structure, and the meaning assigned to each observed relationship.

[[Big Data Management and Processing]] follows data-intensive computation from governance and energy use through memory, scheduling, storage, distributed analytics, security, and domain applications. Its focused topics show how scale changes both technical design and institutional responsibility: systems must move and analyze data efficiently while preserving quality, privacy, trust, financial value, and a defensible connection between a model and the setting where it is used.

[[Data Science Frontiers]] connects data-intensive computing to the legal, philosophical, organizational, and domain questions that determine whether analysis can be trusted and used. Its topics move from individual rights, privacy, and ownership through text analytics, mobile commerce, evidence-based decisions, automated business methods, recommendation, preprocessing, causal inference, and healthcare governance.

chunks.title: Computer Science
chunks.heading: Computer Science > Overview Chapter > From logical rules to system behavior
chunks.content:
[[Biofabrication Systems and Society]] studies engineering with living biological materials. It connects cell culture and biomanufacturing tools with tissue repair, organ models, cellular agriculture, and muscle-powered robots, while treating scale-up, environmental impact, regulation, consent, ownership, and moral status as parts of the design problem. The field shows how an adaptive material changes both what a machine can do and what its creators must govern.

[[Blender 3D Production]] follows digital visual work from an artist's first interaction with Blender to an integrated rendered shot. Its focused topics connect interface organization and three-dimensional navigation to mesh modeling, sculpting, curves, materials, texture coordinates, lighting, keyframe animation, armature rigging, physical simulation, Grease Pencil drawing, rendering, sequence editing, compositing, and camera tracking. The workflow shows how a creative application can keep geometry, time, appearance, physics, and image processing as editable relationships over shared scene data.

[[Bayesian Reasoning and Programming]] expresses uncertain knowledge as executable descriptions paired with explicit inference questions. Its models decompose joint distributions into reusable factors and subprograms, then use exact algebra, numerical methods, sampling, or optimization to answer questions about prediction, diagnosis, control, and learning. The approach makes model incompleteness and computational approximation visible parts of system behavior rather than hidden exceptions to deterministic code.

[[Computational Thinking]] connects the field's methods, machines, institutions, software systems, design practices, scientific uses, education, and emerging architectures. It treats computation both as a way to build machine-realizable capabilities and as a lens for interpreting information processes, while emphasizing that advanced practice is domain-dependent and bounded by mathematical, physical, and social limits. Its focused topics follow computation from the formalization of expert procedures through hardware and large-scale software to human-centered design, simulation, learning systems, and questions about what should be automated.

[[Computing History]] follows the convergence of calculation, storage, control, electronics, communication, and human interaction into modern digital systems. Its topics connect mechanical calculators and punched-card installations to wartime electronic machines, stored programs, mainframes, transistors, integrated circuits, microprocessors, personal computers, graphical interfaces, packet networks, the Web, and mobile social platforms. The history shows that technical capacity alone does not determine adoption: compatibility, public investment, manufacturing knowledge, business models, regulation, communities, and interface design all shape which computational possibilities become durable institutions.

chunks.title: Computer Science
chunks.heading: Computer Science > Overview Chapter > From logical rules to system behavior
chunks.content:
[[Full-Stack Web Application Development]] applies those engineering ideas across a browser client, an HTTP API, server-side application code, persistent data, and production hosting. Its architecture topics explain how Angular components and services coordinate with ASP.NET Core middleware and controllers; its data, form, testing, identity, progressive-web, and deployment topics follow the system from a user's request to stored state and an operational response. The result is not merely a front end placed beside a back end, but a set of explicit contracts whose behavior can be validated at each boundary.

[[Cybersecurity Foundations and Defense]] protects those systems by connecting security goals to cryptography, host isolation, access control, layered monitoring, secure development, and risk analysis. Its topics distinguish threats from vulnerabilities and attacks, follow adversaries through the cyber kill chain, classify malware by propagation and payload, and apply defensive principles to passwords, networks, commerce, blockchains, smart devices, and the Internet of Things. Adaptive and outcome-based methods extend that foundation beyond known signatures toward anomaly detection, resilient service outcomes, and persistent-threat context.

[[C Sharp and .NET Development]] follows one programming ecosystem from language fundamentals to deployed applications. Its focused topics connect C# types, control flow, functions, object design, interfaces, generics, assemblies, packages, runtime data structures, files, cryptography, Entity Framework Core, LINQ, tasks, ASP.NET Core, ML.NET, Windows applications, and Xamarin.Forms mobile clients. The chapter shows how managed execution is organized through nested contracts: types constrain values, libraries define reusable surfaces, serialization and security govern boundaries, and application frameworks coordinate data, concurrency, requests, and user interfaces.

Software changes become a durable shared history through [[Git Version Control]]. Git separates working-tree edits, a staging area, and committed snapshots so a developer can choose a coherent unit of work without recording every local change. Local repositories preserve history and branches offline; remotes provide named exchange points for fetch, pull, and push. Branches are lightweight references to commits, `HEAD` identifies the checked-out history position, and merges connect independent lines of work. These mechanisms make collaboration inspectable: status shows present state, logs show recorded decisions, and conflicts identify places where integration requires human judgment.

The behavior of a program also depends on how its parts interact. [[Systems Foundations]] introduces boundaries, state, hierarchy, models, and the distinction between a system and its environment. [[System Dynamics]] then explains change through stocks, flows, feedback loops, delays, and nonlinear relationships. A reinforcing loop can amplify growth, while a balancing loop can stabilize a system around a target. When many local interactions produce a global pattern that was not directly specified, the result belongs to [[Emergent Systems]]. Emergence reminds us that understanding every component separately may not be enough to predict the behavior of the whole.

chunks.title: Computer Science
chunks.heading: Computer Science > Overview Chapter > From logical rules to system behavior
chunks.content: Computational behavior ultimately meets human interpretation. [[Human Cognition]] covers perception, attention, memory, reasoning, skill acquisition, and cognitive load. These capacities determine what people notice, remember, misunderstand, or learn when using a system. Computer science therefore cannot treat the user as an interchangeable input device: the design of representations and controls must account for the strengths and limits of human information processing.

chunks.title: Computer Science
chunks.heading: Computer Science > Overview Chapter > Interaction expands the system boundary
chunks.content:
[[Interaction Design]] treats the exchange between person and machine as a reciprocal loop. An interface presents possible actions, receives input, changes system state, and provides feedback that helps the user decide what to do next. Good interaction depends on a clear conceptual model and short semantic and articulatory distances between a person's goal and the operations supplied by the interface. [[UX Evaluation]] tests whether those relationships actually work through task analysis, usability inspection, walkthroughs, formative studies, and summative measurement.

When interaction moves beyond a flat screen, spatial perception becomes part of computation. [[Spatial Perception and Navigation]] explains depth cues, orientation, cognitive maps, landmarks, and route finding, while [[Spatial Interaction]] turns those abilities into techniques for selecting, positioning, rotating, scaling, traveling, and controlling systems in three dimensions. [[Augmented Reality Systems]] connects those foundations to physical environments through XR displays, spatial tracking, computer vision, registration, visual coherence, situated visualization, tangible interaction, authoring, navigation, collaboration, and distributed real-time architecture. An augmentation succeeds only when the entire perception-action loop keeps digital information meaningfully aligned with a changing world.

chunks.title: Computer Science
chunks.heading: Computer Science > Overview Chapter > Learning, speech, and conversational machines
chunks.content:
Some computational problems are too variable to solve with an exhaustive collection of hand-written rules. [[Machine Learning and Neural Networks]] addresses them by fitting models to examples or rewards. Supervised learning uses labeled data, unsupervised learning searches for latent structure, and reinforcement learning improves a policy through consequences. Neural architectures add layers, recurrence, attention, convolution, and memory mechanisms that can learn complex mappings from large datasets.

Speech illustrates why data-driven modeling matters. [[Speech and Acoustic Modeling]] represents a changing waveform as short frames and feature vectors, then relates that evidence to phonetic units, pronunciations, and probable word sequences. [[Speech Recognition Systems]] use these representations to convert speech into text across speakers, accents, vocabularies, and acoustic conditions. Recognition determines what words were spoken, but it does not determine what those words mean.

That interpretive step belongs to [[Natural Language Understanding Systems]]. An assistant can classify an intent, extract entities, and assemble them into a meaning representation defined by a domain schema or ontology. The [[Dialog Management Systems]] layer combines that representation with conversational and personal context, selects the next action, resolves references, requests missing information, and recovers from ambiguity or errors. Once an action or result is ready, [[Language and Speech Generation]] plans the response, realizes it as text, predicts pronunciation and prosody, and may synthesize a spoken waveform.

[[Virtual Assistant Architecture]] joins recognition, understanding, dialog, generation, and external digital services into a modular pipeline. Architecture alone does not make the interaction natural. [[Conversational Assistant Design]] governs prompts, initiative, turn-taking, multimodality, proactivity, personality, and social expectations. A capable assistant must coordinate its technical modules while making uncertainty, available actions, privacy boundaries, and conversational control legible to the user.

The effects of computational systems cannot be separated from their capabilities. [[AI Ethics]] connects the design and deployment of intelligent systems to questions about human identity, machine moral status, data power, responsibility, explainability, fairness, governance, labor, and environmental sustainability. It treats an AI application as part of a larger sociotechnical system whose outcomes depend on institutions, infrastructure, and the distribution of power as well as code and models.

chunks.title: Computer Science
chunks.heading: Computer Science > Overview Chapter > Games as computational systems
chunks.content:
[[Game Programming]] describes the implementation layer that keeps an interactive game running coherently in real time. Its focused topics connect frame timing and object architecture to 2D and 3D rendering, spatial mathematics, device input, audio, collision and movement, cameras, game AI, interface code, scripting, data formats, and network protocols. The chapter makes the dependencies among those systems explicit: a coordinate-space convention can affect rendering, audio, physics, cameras, and picking, while update order and authority determine whether local and networked state remain consistent.

Games provide a concentrated example of computation, systems, interaction, and experience working together. [[Game Foundations]] organizes the defining structures and expressive forms of games. [[Game Systems]] examines the parts, attributes, resources, engines, ecologies, and progression structures that generate gameplay, while [[Game Interactivity]] focuses on the reciprocal loop through which player action changes the game and feedback changes later action.

The system becomes meaningful only through a player. [[Player Experience Design]] connects goals, motivation, challenge, flow, fun, mental models, onboarding, and different styles of play. These desired experiences do not follow automatically from a rule set. [[Game Design Methods]] supplies concept statements, prototypes, design documents, playtests, and iterative methods that let a team explore the relationship between rules and experience before committing to a complete production.

Several specialized areas make those relationships measurable and tunable. [[Game Economies]] studies resources, currencies, production, exchange, sources, sinks, prices, inflation, and stagnation. [[Game Balance and Progression]] asks how costs, benefits, difficulty, pacing, and advancement can preserve meaningful choices over time. [[Game Analytics and Probability]] adds probability distributions, random systems, quantitative models, cohorts, retention, and behavioral data. Together, these topics show that balance is neither purely mathematical nor purely intuitive: models propose relationships, play reveals actual behavior, and evidence guides revision.

chunks.title: Computer Science
chunks.heading: Computer Science > Overview Chapter > Organizing the work
chunks.content:
Large computational systems require a development process that can learn while delivering. [[Scrum and Agile Foundations]] describes empirical development, agile values, product ownership, facilitation, and self-managing cross-discipline teams. [[Scrum Iteration Practices]] turns those principles into timeboxed goals, planning, daily coordination, review, and retrospective adaptation. [[Agile Backlog and Estimation]] connects user needs to ordered work through user stories, acceptance criteria, refinement, relative estimates, and release forecasts.

Process also depends on people and organizational structure. [[Agile Team Leadership]] emphasizes coaching, facilitation, psychological safety, shared accountability, and leadership adapted to a team's situation. [[Scaling Agile Teams]] addresses communication overhead, feature and component structures, integration, dependencies, and coordination across many teams. In the specialized setting of [[Game Production]], these practices meet creative vision, scope, milestones, stage gates, quality assurance, live operations, and release constraints.

chunks.title: Computer Science
chunks.heading: Computer Science > Overview Chapter > Computing delivered as services
chunks.content: [[Cloud Computing]] reorganizes infrastructure, platforms, software, information, and business processes as measured services reached through networks. Virtualization and resource pools enable elastic capacity, while public, private, community, and hybrid models define who shares it. Reusable service cells, catalogs, brokers, and integration contracts let organizations compose capabilities across providers. Pricing and financial models connect those capabilities to business value; security, continuity, backup, interoperability, and governance keep abstraction from hiding accountability. Cloud adoption therefore changes not only where computation runs but how it is purchased, controlled, recovered, and woven into work.

chunks.title: Computer Science
chunks.heading: Computer Science > Overview Chapter > Discovering structure in data
chunks.content:
[[Cluster Analysis and Data Mining]] follows the complete path from representing observations to interpreting discovered structure. Proximity measures, hierarchical trees, partition methods, fuzzy membership, classification, association rules, categorical algorithms, density models, probability mixtures, and neural maps provide different ways to expose regularity. Data preparation determines what those methods can see, while stability checks, simulations, recovery indices, and domain interpretation determine whether their output is credible. The chapter treats a clustering as an evidence-bearing model shaped by its data, objective, parameters, and intended use.

[[Digital Image Forensics]] models the physical and computational history of a photograph so that claims about authenticity can be tested against evidence. Its focused topics compare metadata, exposure, lighting, perspective, JPEG encoding, duplicated or resampled pixels, color-filter interpolation, sensor fingerprints, and physiological video signals. The field shows how computation can recover subtle traces that human vision misses while also demanding cautious interpretation: post-processing can resemble tampering, detectors depend on explicit assumptions, and a failure to find an anomaly can never prove that an image is authentic.

Across all of these areas, computer science moves repeatedly between abstraction and experience. Logic supplies precision; engineering makes change manageable; systems thinking exposes interactions; human cognition and interface design connect computation to people; machine learning handles variation; and production practices turn uncertain ideas into maintained artifacts. The field is unified less by a single technology than by this disciplined movement from representations and models to behavior, evidence, and revision.
